findings.title: Enforce the 10 MB source limit on the server before image processing
findings.body: The new 10 MB limit exists only in browser JavaScript and does not apply to direct multipart requests. Any image body accepted by the proxy, regardless of its source size, reaches this block and is sent through up to five ImageMagick/ImageOptim conversions before Upload.create_for can apply its normal final-size validation. An authenticated caller can bypass the client check with a very large or decompression-bomb image and consume substantial worker CPU, memory, and disk. Reject source files above the intended input limit in the controller before invoking OptimizedImage.downsize.

findings.title: The new downsize definition replaces the existing width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature, so this second def self.downsize replaces the preceding def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}). Existing callers using the old four-argument form bind max_height as opts and then fail when optimize evaluates opts[:allow_animation]; callers passing the optional fifth argument raise ArgumentError. Preserve both call forms in a single method or use a differently named percentage-based helper.

findings.title: Client validation now ignores the configured per-type upload limits
findings.body: This replaces max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb with a universal 10 MB limit for both images and attachments. Consequently, attachments larger than a site's configured attachment limit are allowed through the UI only to fail on the server, while files that a site explicitly permits above 10 MB are rejected in the browser. The image-source allowance needed for downscaling should be applied only to images; attachment validation must continue to use max_attachment_size_kb.

findings.title: Downsizing can irreversibly turn uploaded animated GIFs into single-frame GIFs
findings.body: When allow_animated_thumbnails is false, this call selects OptimizedImage's non-animated downsize path, whose ImageMagick input is tempfile.path[0] and therefore contains only the first GIF frame. The result is then passed to Upload.create_for as the original upload, not merely as a generated thumbnail, so an oversized animated GIF is permanently stored as a static image. Skip animated uploads when animation-preserving conversion is disabled, or always use an animation-preserving path for the original upload.

findings.title: Five fixed resize attempts do not ensure the final upload meets the configured limit
findings.body: The loop limits itself to five 80% dimension reductions, but file byte size is content-dependent and max_image_size_kb is configurable. For example, a 10 MB source with a low configured limit can still exceed that limit after five passes, and a re-encode can reduce less than expected. The code then submits the still-oversized tempfile to Upload.create_for, causing the upload to be rejected despite the feature promising automatic reduction. Continue until the file meets the limit or no further reduction is possible, and handle a failed downsize explicitly.
